{{Short description|German science writer}}
'''Jörg Blech''' (born 1966) is a German science journalist and nonfiction author.

He is known primarily as a critic of the healthcare and pharmaceutical industries.  His books cover such subjects as the healthcare industry's alleged invention of diseases to generate sales and medical treatments that turned out to harm people.

He studied [[biology]] and [[biochemistry]] in [[Germany]] and [[United Kingdom|Britain]]. In addition to his books, which have been translated into [[English language|English]], [[French language|French]], [[Italian language|Italian]], [[Spanish language|Spanish]], [[Dutch language|Dutch]], [[Finnish language|Finnish]], [[Hungarian language|Hungarian]], [[Polish language|Polish]], [[Chinese language|Chinese]] and [[Korean language|Korean]],<ref>[http://www.worldcat.org/search?qt=worldcat_org_all&q=Jörg+Blech Worldcat]</ref>  he writes for the German publication [[Der Spiegel]]. His book, ''Inventing Disease and Pushing Pills: Pharmaceutical Companies and the Medicalisation of Normal Life'',<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=y67uAAAAMAAJ ''Inventing Disease and Pushing Pills: Pharmaceutical Companies and the Medicalisation of Normal Life''], Routledge, 2006</ref>  was reviewed by several journals.<ref>''Health & Social Care in the Community,'' 15, no. 4 (2007): 391-392</ref><ref>''Health Promotion Journal of Australia'', 19, no. 1, (2008): 74</ref>
